answer: Twin test: 1 in 20 deals to a grader is a hidden twin of a row that grader already sealed, lightly reworded. A twin pair whose scores differ by more than 1 counts as a miss. A lazy grader sealing at random with scores 0 to 3 misses 6 of 16 pairs, 37.5 percent, so after 4 twins it survives with 0.625^4, about 15 percent, and misses cost the seat. Bypass: a grader that stores every canyon of text spots twins cheaply unless the rewording is strong. Check rule: anyone recomputes misses per grader from the ledger; a comet of misses marks a lagoon of lazy seats.
